aquabirnaviral isolates differ in their cytopathogenicity, ability to replicate, and ability to induce apoptosis or gene expression.
the genetic and serological diversity of aquabivnaviruses is reflected in their ability to induce cyto-pathogenic effects in-vitro.

the infection profiles induced by selected aquabirnaviral isolates differ in terms of virus loads and ability of these isolates to induce cytopatic effects, apoptosis, and IFNa, MxA1, PKR, or TNFa gene expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and identification of the molecular and cellular mechanisms of infection of different aquabirnaviral isolates.
the identification of molecular mechanisms that are involved in the induction of cytopathogenic effects and host response in aquabirnaviral infections in fish.
understanding the mechanisms by which different aquabirnaviral isolates interact with the host cell and the factors that may influence the outcome of infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
each aquabirnaviral isolate is a unique virus with a unique infection profile.
aquabirnaviral isolates are genetically and functionally diverse and therefore require further studies to understand their pathogenesis and epidemiology.
aquabirnaviral isolates have unique infection profiles and that the differences observed in this study could be attributed to the genetic diversity of the isolates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the infection profiles of aquabirnnavirus isolates are isolate specific.
the infection profiles induced in-vitro by different aquabirnaviral isolates vary with respect to their ability to replicate and induce gene expression.
the infection profiles of aquabiraviruses are not only dependent on the genetic make-up but are also influenced by the environment and host.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aquabirnaviral infection profiles are complex and should be studied in a holistic manner.
the host response to infection is not uniform and may be influenced by factors such as genetic identity, serotype and genotype, host and environmental conditions.
the use of a single isolate for studies on aquabirnaviral pathogenicity may lead to erroneous results.
